# Confirmation commitment and retry logic

# Confirmation commitment and retry logic — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Confirmation commitment and retry logic. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] A null entry from getSignatureStatuses means the status was not found, not that the transaction failed. The method searches only a recent status cache unless searchTransactionHistory is true. A null can mean dropped, never landed, or evicted from the cache. Treat the transaction as dead only after block height passes lastValidBlockHeight and a history search also returns null. (medium confidence) — https://www.helius.dev/docs/rpc/guides/getsignaturestatuses.md · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://github.com/fardream/confirm-solana-transaction

## How it works

- [statement] A successful sendTransaction response returns only a signature. It does not show that the cluster will process or finalize the transaction. The caller must poll getSignatureStatuses, because the RPC can return a signature for a transaction that is later dropped. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://onfinality.io/en/learn/solana-rpc-timeout-and-retries
- [statement] Fetching a blockhash at processed can pick a blockhash from a minority fork that the cluster later abandons. The transaction is then dropped with the blockhash not found. Official docs advise confirmed or finalized when polling getLatestBlockhash. Helius calls confirmed the best practice for sending and states that processed is not recommended for production-critical flows. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://www.helius.dev/blog/solana-commitment-levels, https://www.helius.dev/blog/how-to-deal-with-blockhash-errors-on-solana
- [statement] sendTransaction returns only the transaction id (the first signature). A successful response says nothing about whether the cluster will process or finalize the transaction, and the RPC can hand back a signature for a transaction that is later dropped. A bot must poll getSignatureStatuses to learn the outcome. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://onfinality.io/en/learn/solana-rpc-timeout-and-retries, https://www.helius.dev/docs/rpc/guides/getsignaturestatuses.md
- [statement] A fee-bumped rebroadcast is a different transaction. Changing the compute-unit price changes the message, so the message hash and signature change and the AlreadyProcessed check does not link the two. RPC Fast describes rebroadcasting 'with a slightly higher priority fee' when a transaction is not processed within 2 slots. By the official guide's logic both versions can land while the blockhash is valid. Guard such intents on-chain (Circuit added a sequence-enforcer instruction with TTL checks) or accept duplicates. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/v4.4.0/runtime/src/bank/check_transactions.rs · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx, https://rpcfast.com/blog/how-to-land-transactions-solana, https://circuittrading.notion.site/November-10-2024-JLP-Vaults-Post-Mortem-13b1385fd0f58031b7acde64235c4852
- [statement] Two intentionally identical transactions collide. The duplicate check keys on the whole message hash, so the same fee payer, instructions, accounts and blockhash give AlreadyProcessed on the second send. Change the message (a fresh blockhash or different instruction data) to send a distinct second transaction. Chainstack also warns that transactions can be treated as duplicates when many share a blockhash. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/v4.4.0/runtime/src/bank/check_transactions.rs · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error
- [statement] Do not re-sign with a new blockhash while the first blockhash can still land. The Solana retry guide calls confirming expiry first 'very important' because both transactions can be accepted. Chainstack and the fardream library say the same. The safe order: rebroadcast identical bytes until block height is past lastValidBlockHeight, make a final status lookup, then rebuild. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error, https://github.com/fardream/confirm-solana-transaction

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Commitment guidance changed with Alpenglow. The Solana docs say to point new code at finalized, because it now arrives in about 150 ms, and to re-check every timeout, retry or UX delay tuned to 12.8-second finality. They say confirmed will be removed in a later release. Triton One warns not to move to finalized before the node runs Alpenglow, or requests wait the old 12.8 s. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/media/content/upgrades/alpenglow.mdx · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://blog.triton.one/alpenglow-and-your-triton-stack-what-to-update-before-mainnet/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Resending identical signed bytes is harmless because the network executes at most one copy of a given signature. The duplicate risk comes only from building a second, different transaction. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/fardream/confirm-solana-transaction · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx
- [statement] Once a blockhash has expired, resending the same signed bytes cannot succeed: the handler must fetch a fresh blockhash, re-sign and resend, and a generic HTTP retry wrapper does not do that. Retries consume blockhashes and can cost fees, and no retry strategy rescues a badly degraded network, so fail fast and alert. (medium confidence) — https://onfinality.io/en/learn/solana-rpc-timeout-and-retries · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error
- [statement] One web3.js user reported confirmTransaction throwing the block-height-exceeded error for a transaction that had already finalized, after sending with a confirmed blockhash and confirming at confirmed. The issue tracker bot closed it by pointing to the Agave repo, and no cause was recorded. Treat an expiry exception as a prompt to check the signature status before rebuilding. (low confidence) — https://github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/35556
- [statement] Rebroadcasting identical signed bytes cannot execute twice. Agave's check_transactions rejects a message hash that is already in the StatusCache with AlreadyProcessed ('This transaction has already been processed'). The cost is an error, not a double spend. With preflight on, sendTransaction runs a simulation and returns any simulation error, so a Drift keeper-bot log shows 'Transaction simulation failed: This transaction has already been processed'. A rebroadcast loop must treat that error as 'look up the signature', not as failure. Re-sending with skipPreflight true, as the Solana guide's example does, avoids the error. (high confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/6cd331bf6fd0e92c59e847a3aefaac16ff7b7eda/runtime/src/bank/check_transactions.rs · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/6cd331bf6fd0e92c59e847a3aefaac16ff7b7eda/rpc/src/rpc.rs, https://github.com/drift-labs/keeper-bots-v2/issues/130, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] 'Transaction simulation failed: This transaction has already been processed' on a resend means an identical message is already in the status cache. Read the signature's status instead of treating the send as failed. A Drift keeper bot logged that error and then failed with a 30-second 'not confirmed' timeout; a Drift maintainer attributed this class of error to congestion or an RPC node that fell behind. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/drift-labs/keeper-bots-v2/issues/130 · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/v4.4.0/runtime/src/bank/check_transactions.rs

## Facts and statements

- [statement] A blockhash is valid for about 150 blocks. The sources quote this window as roughly 1 minute 19 seconds, 60-90 seconds, or 80-90 seconds, depending on slot time. A transaction not processed in that window must be rebuilt with a new blockhash. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://www.helius.dev/blog/how-to-deal-with-blockhash-errors-on-solana, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error
- [statement] Re-sign with a new blockhash only after the current block height exceeds lastValidBlockHeight. Before then, the original transaction may still land, and a re-signed copy with a different blockhash is a distinct transaction that can also execute. The user then sees the same action twice. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://github.com/fardream/confirm-solana-transaction, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error
- [statement] Do not re-sign with a new blockhash until the original blockhash has expired. While it is still valid, both transactions can be accepted, and the user sees the same action twice. Re-sign only after the block height passes lastValidBlockHeight. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error, https://github.com/fardream/confirm-solana-transaction
- [statement] Do not treat a processed status as done. The retry guide documents a transaction that a leader on a minority fork processed and that was dropped before it finalized, and the Solana docs say processed data can change if the cluster switches forks. Under Alpenglow processed is unchanged and means only that a bank executed the transaction. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Confirmation commitment and retry logic · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/rpc/http/sendtransaction.mdx, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/media/content/upgrades/alpenglow.mdx
